ryan-release: quick q — for the tiny infra patches that only touch lockfiles or CI glue, are we comfortable doing a micro/metadata-only bump (e.g. 1.2.3+meta or 1.2.3-micro) to avoid implying a patch semver change? or should we always bump patch for any repo change?
mei-engineering: leaning micro-only for lockfile churn. patch bumps cause a bunch of downstream releases and changelog noise.
sasha: +1 micro for pure lockfile updates. as long as we document it in release notes that it is non-behavioral.
jamie: worried about package registries and consumers — do tooling ecosystems treat build/metadata suffixes consistently? npm/pypi might ignore metadata in semver sorting.
ryan-release: good point. npm ignores +build metadata when comparing versions (semver spec). maybe use a dash pre-release like `1.2.3-micro.1` so it sorts before `1.2.4`?
mei-engineering: I tested a couple repos: npm treats `1.2.3+lock` same as `1.2.3` for range resolution. pip/poetry treat local version identifiers differently. so we risk surprises for Python packages.
jamie: hmm. then maybe default to patch bumps for published libraries and allow micro metadata-only tags for internal infra repos and tools we control.
sasha: that sounds reasonable. can we formalize policy:
- published libs (package index or client-facing): always semver patch for anything in repo
- internal infra / infra tooling + repo-scoped lockfile fixes: allowed micro metadata tags, with changelog entry and explicit note in release notes
- CI/bot-only changes that do not affect artifacts: skip release entirely if possible (or tag `skip-release`)
ryan-release: draft rule sounds good. one more: if a "micro" change is later found to affect runtime, we must re-release with a proper patch and update downstreams — mark as "possible backport" in notes.
ci-bot: automated check available: `release-policy/lint` will flag repos missing a release when package files changed. we can add a rule to require patch bump for published packages.
deploy-bot: deploy log: canary deploy queued for v1.2.3-micro.1 -> rejecting; registry policy: publishing blocked for pre-release tags without `--allow-prerelease` (info).
ryan-release: thanks deploy-bot — that confirms we should avoid `+build` metadata for published npm packages. propose: use `patch` for published, `-micro.N` for internal, and `skip-release` label for pure CI script tweaks.
mei-engineering: I'll open a tiny RFC in repo infra explaining the three-case rule, include examples and a small script to classify repos by "published" vs "internal".
jamie: can we also add the rollback guidance? e.g., if we accidentally publish a micro as a patch, how we roll back (yank, deprecate, republish) — add step-by-step.
sasha: yep. put a short checklist: yank -> republish patched version -> notify slack + changelog update.
ryan-release: ok, action items: Mei to write RFC, me to update release bot lint rules, Jamie to draft rollback checklist. ping me when RFC ready and we'll ship policy. :thumbsup:
mei-engineering: on it. will cc you.
ci-bot: note: `release-policy/lint` ticket created #4321 (automated).
ryan-release: thanks all. closing thread.
